_readme: Hand-authored structures for the molecules of one patent that resolve_structures.py
cannot get any other way. One entry per MOLECULE, keyed by an exact identifier string
from gold/compounds.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: 0 of the 75 compound records carry smiles, inchi or
molecular_formula, and gold/structures.json only covers what the patent DRAWS. Every
reagent that is named but never drawn (methanesulfonyl chloride, thionyl chloride,
triethylamine and the rest) has no structure anywhere in the pipeline, and half of them
carry a mass/mole pair that the downstream mass-balance check cannot use without a
formula. Those are the entries below.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE: spelling variants. The pipeline already knows that
'2-chloro-6-(methanesulfonyl)toluene' and '2-chloro-6-(methylsulfonyl)toluene' are one
molecule, because finalise.py wrote that out to provenance/compounds-equivalence.json.
resolve_structures.py propagates a structure across each equivalence group and tags the
copies origin 'derived'. Write one entry, for one spelling, and let it propagate. The
optional 'aliases' list is only for synonyms the equivalence index misses, such as
'anhydrous aluminium trichloride' against 'aluminium trichloride'.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE EITHER: molecules the patent draws. Those come out of
gold/structures.json with origin 'patent_drawing', which is a stronger provenance claim
than 'curated'. An entry here for a drawn molecule is harmless (the join is on RDKit
canonical SMILES, so it lands on the same molecule and keeps the stronger origin) but it
is work you did not need to do.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: 'cyclohexanedione' (Claims). The gold records it resolved:false
because the patent prints it with no ring locants, so which isomer is meant is not
stated. Supplying the 1,3-dione here would silently resolve what the annotator
deliberately left open. It gets origin 'none'. Same for the unresolved Chinese class
terms, and for water, HCl, MgSO4 and the other trivial reagents, which carry no
chemistry and are noise when drawn.
FIELDS: 'smiles' is required and must parse in RDKit. 'slug' is optional and names the
SVG file; omit it and one is derived from the identifier. 'aliases' and 'note' are
optional. formula, mw and canonical are NOT stored here: resolve_structures.py computes
them with RDKit on every run and writes them into gold/structures-resolved.json, so
there is one place they can be wrong instead of two.
Every SMILES below was checked atom by atom against its IUPAC name before it was
committed. A wrong structure here silently corrupts a mass-balance check downstream.

ruthenium oxide.note: Ruthenium(IV) oxide, RuO2. THE PATENT SAYS SO IN WORDS: line 109 reads 'in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst', and line 185 adds 'ruthenium dioxide and ruthenium dioxide hydrate'. Curated because the bare name 'ruthenium oxide' is ambiguous and the two automated readers split on it: OPSIN parsed it as RuO and PubChem returned RuO2. The patent's own arithmetic settles it independently of both: Example 1 at line 264 charges 1.5 g as 0.011 mol, which is 136 g/mol. RuO2 is 133.07 and RuO is 117.07.
